label: Wildfire and power shutoff response
description: The organizations whose job is wildfire in the wildland-urban interface: a fire district or agency, a county wildfire and evacuation program (emergency management with the sheriff), or an electric utility's wildfire and public safety power shutoff program. Plans and products: the community wildfire protection plan, evacuation zone maps and the county alert and warning plan, incident status summaries, the utility wildfire mitigation plan with its shutoff notification schedule, and smoke guidance from public health. Variants: a fire district or agency (incident command, dispatch, planning), a county wildfire and evacuation program (emergency manager, sheriff, public information) and a utility wildfire and power shutoff program (shutoff incident commander, meteorology, customer care). Red flag warnings and fire weather products come from the weather toolkit; the flooding toolkit supplies the flood side of burn scar floods.

vocabulary.facility: the fire district or the county's evacuation zones and roads, or the utility's circuits, substations and community resource centers
vocabulary.public: residents in the wildland-urban interface, medical baseline customers, campers, school families and care home residents
vocabulary.frontline: engine and crew bosses, dispatchers, deputies running zone sweeps, line crews and patrol staff, utility customer care agents
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the incident command post, the county emergency operations center (EOC) or the utility's emergency operations center

it: incident command post software and the incident log
county mapping system with evacuation zones, parcels and critical facilities
alert and warning platform with Wireless Emergency Alert access
evacuation zone map for the public
utility outage management and customer information system
customer notification system for calls, texts and email
weather station network and fire potential models
email and the county or district website
ot: utility SCADA and the distribution management system
water system pumps and tank levels
variable message signs and road closure gates

roles.name: Fire Incident Commander
roles.description: Owns strategy, tactics, resource orders and the request for evacuation.

roles.name: Planning Section Chief / Fire Behavior Analyst
roles.description: Owns spread projections, perimeters and the timing of the threat to each zone.

roles.name: Dispatch / Coordination Center Manager
roles.description: Owns resource orders, mutual aid and the effects of the national preparedness level.

roles.name: Sheriff or Police Incident Commander
roles.description: Owns evacuation orders and warnings, zone sweeps, road control and contraflow.

roles.name: County Emergency Manager
roles.description: Owns alert and warning, shelters, animal and access and functional needs support and requests to the state.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Owns messages that match the status of each zone, rumor control and coordination with the utility.

roles.name: Utility Wildfire / Power Shutoff Incident Commander
roles.description: Owns the decision to de-energize and re-energize, the circuits, the customers and the notifications.

roles.name: Utility Meteorologist / Fire Potential Analyst
roles.description: Owns fuel and wind forecasts, circuit-level risk and the timing of the event window.

roles.name: Utility Customer Care and Community Liaison
roles.description: Owns notices to customers and public safety partners, medical baseline outreach and community resource centers.

roles.name: Public Health Officer
roles.description: Owns smoke advisories, clean-air shelters and guidance for schools and events.

outsideParties: the National Weather Service forecast office and its fire weather desk
the geographic area coordination center and the National Interagency Coordination Center
state emergency management and the state fire agency
the state department of transportation and highway patrol
airports and the FAA (temporary flight restrictions)
the air quality agency (EPA and the state district)
volunteer organizations active in disaster and animal rescue groups
the electric utility's public safety partner liaison
mediaChannels: a resident's video of flames on a ridge posted to Facebook and Nextdoor
a post on X/Twitter naming zones that are not under order
the regional TV station's fire map
the county emergency management Facebook page

sceneAnchors.public: on a suburban street at dusk: an orange sky, ash falling, cars loaded with belongings, a deputy waving traffic, a brush-covered hillside beyond the fences
sceneAnchors.control: inside a county emergency operations center: a wall map with colored evacuation zones, laptops, a whiteboard of road closures and shelters, staff with radios, fluorescent light
sceneAnchors.exterior: on a hillside road: a fire engine with lights on, hose lines, a smoke column above a ridge, dry grass and oak brush, a utility pole with a line crew truck

addedThreatFamilies.label: Wildland-urban interface fire
addedThreatFamilies.description: A fast wind-driven fire reaches homes in pre-defined evacuation zones; orders and warnings must go out before the fire arrives less the zone's clearance time, and every partner's message must match the same zone map.

phaseArc.title: Red flag forecast and ignition
phaseArc.goal: Players see a red flag warning and a first report of smoke, and decide how early to stage resources and pre-alert zones.
beats: A red flag warning is in effect with gusts forecast above the usual
A caller reports smoke on a ridge above a subdivision
Initial attack engines are dispatched and the first size-up is radioed

phaseArc.title: Extended attack and rapid growth
phaseArc.goal: The fire outruns initial attack; the projected arrival at the first zones is shorter than the clearance time, so the call on warnings and orders is time critical.
beats: The incident commander reports spotting ahead of the head of the fire
The planning section projects arrival at Zone 3 in about 90 minutes
The sheriff asks whether to order Zone 3 now or warn first

phaseArc.title: Orders, evacuation and road constraints
phaseArc.goal: Orders reach zones through several channels while a canyon road, a care home and large animals complicate the movement.
beats: A zone order goes out by alert platform, text and door-to-door sweeps
A single-lane road backs up and contraflow is weighed
A care home needs transport and a school bus route crosses the fire zone

phaseArc.title: Shelters, containment and re-entry
phaseArc.goal: Shelters, animal shelters and re-entry rules are managed while partners repeat the right zone status and a burn scar flood watch follows.
beats: Shelters near capacity and an animal shelter opens
Containment rises and zones step down from order to warning
Residents ask when they can return and rumors list the wrong zones

decisionPointExamples: order Zone 3 now on the projected arrival, or warn first and risk an order that comes too late
open contraflow on the canyon road and lose the engine access, or keep one lane for responders
move the care home before the order, or shelter in place with a generator that has four hours of fuel
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a spot fire ahead of the head, a wind shift forecast, an engine boss's size-up that differs from the planning section's projection, a zone map that the alert platform shows differently
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a canyon road that backs up, a zone with no cell coverage, a siren that does not reach the drainage, an alert platform that rejects the zone polygon, a hydrant system that loses pressure
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the sheriff or police incident commander (who issues orders) and the fire incident commander (who projects arrival)
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Use zone ids exactly as listed in the project's facts and the same status words on the map, the table and every message (evacuation order, evacuation warning, shelter in place, none). A perimeter is a mapped polygon at a time, not continuous truth. Acreage and containment percent have fixed meanings. Times are local with a time zone. Do not predict fire behavior beyond the case data; the projected arrival comes from the scenario's case data.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Red flag wind event and power shutoff
addedThreatFamilies.description: High wind and dry fuels lead a utility to consider a public safety power shutoff; partners and customers must be notified inside their windows and the people who depend on power must be reached.

phaseArc.title: Forecast and watch
phaseArc.goal: The utility sees a wind and fuel forecast and decides whether to call a watch and notify public safety partners 48 to 72 hours ahead.
beats: The utility meteorologist flags a wind event above the circuit thresholds
The fire potential index reaches the top class on several circuits
The watch call is held and partners ask for the circuit list

phaseArc.title: Notification windows
phaseArc.goal: Partner and customer notices must go out inside their windows; medical baseline and critical facility customers need extra contact.
beats: The partner notice goes to the county and the fire district
Customer notices begin 24 to 48 hours ahead
A hospital and a water pump station ask for the schedule and a generator plan

phaseArc.title: De-energization
phaseArc.goal: The decision to de-energize is made against the event window; the 1 to 4 hour and power-off notices go out and the community resource center opens.
beats: Gusts cross the threshold on three circuits
The decision to de-energize is called and the 1 to 4 hour notices go out
Residents on well pumps and oxygen concentrators call the utility

phaseArc.title: Restoration and report
phaseArc.goal: Patrols clear circuits for restoration in sequence; restoration times, complaints and notification records feed the post-event report.
beats: Winds fall below the threshold and patrols begin
Restoration is sequenced and some circuits wait for patrol results
The post-event report lists customers, durations and notification times

decisionPointExamples: call the shutoff on circuits 12 and 14 now, or wait for the next forecast and shorten the 1 to 4 hour notice
re-energize a circuit before patrol finishes because a hospital is on generator power
send the partner notice at 40 hours when the decision is uncertain, or at 60 hours when the forecast is firmer
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a forecast update with higher gusts, a station reading ahead of the forecast, a medical baseline list that differs from the customer list, a patrol report of a downed conductor
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a notification system that fails to send a batch, a call center that cannot reach customers without a number, a hospital whose generator will not start, a cell site on battery power
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the county emergency management and the fire district (public safety partners), and critical facility customers
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Notification windows are 48 to 72 hours for public safety partners, 24 to 48 hours for customers, 1 to 4 hours before if possible, and at de-energization; the project may change them (they are California's example rule, not a national requirement). All customers, circuits and facilities are fictional. Counts must add up across circuits, classes and the medical baseline list.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Smoke and air quality episode
addedThreatFamilies.description: Wildfire smoke raises the Air Quality Index at hospitals, schools and events; facilities decide on shelter, filtration, closure and cancellation against thresholds that are local plans.

phaseArc.title: Haze and first readings
phaseArc.goal: A smoke plume moves toward town and readings begin to rise; facilities check their plans.
beats: A smoke advisory is issued for the county
The AQI reaches Moderate then Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups
A school asks whether to hold recess indoors

phaseArc.title: Thresholds crossed
phaseArc.goal: The AQI crosses the thresholds that the local plans name; decisions on filtration, closures and events fall due.
beats: The AQI crosses 150 and a district threshold for early release
A hospital sees more respiratory visits
An outdoor event organizer asks for a decision

phaseArc.title: Peak and shelter decisions
phaseArc.goal: Smoke peaks; clean-air shelters open and messages must agree across health, schools and the county.
beats: The AQI reaches Very Unhealthy for several hours
A clean-air shelter opens in a library
Messages disagree about which schools are closed

phaseArc.title: Clearing and recovery
phaseArc.goal: The air clears slowly; reopening and communication end the episode.
beats: The AQI falls into Moderate overnight
Schools plan reopening and make-up days
The health officer reviews the advisory

decisionPointExamples: close schools at 150 or wait for the afternoon forecast
cancel the outdoor festival on a forecast, or hold it with masks and a clean-air tent
move elective procedures at the hospital or keep the schedule with filtration
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an AQI forecast update, a sensor that reads higher than the reporting area, a smoke polygon that shifts, a hospital emergency department visit count
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a school air handling system that cannot take a higher filter, a shelter with no staff, a sensor outage, a bus route through the smoke
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the public health officer and the school district or hospital
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Use the EPA PM2.5 Air Quality Index categories and breakpoints in effect since 6 May 2024 and always give the category name beside the number. Thresholds for schools and events are local plans, not federal rules.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Wildfire resource shortage
addedThreatFamilies.description: Many fires burn at once; engines, crews and aircraft are committed elsewhere, mutual aid is slow and the incident must decide what to protect with what it has.

phaseArc.title: Competing incidents
phaseArc.goal: The coordination center reports many fires and a rising preparedness level.
beats: The preparedness level rises to 4
A resource order is filled in part
A neighboring county commits its engines

phaseArc.title: Orders go unfilled
phaseArc.goal: Orders sit unfilled and the incident must prioritize structures.
beats: Requested strike teams are not available
The incident commander asks for a priority list
Structure triage moves to the north side

phaseArc.title: Prioritization and public messages
phaseArc.goal: Players decide what to protect first and the public message must be truthful about resources.
beats: The sheriff asks about earlier warnings for zones that lose protection
A reporter asks why engines left
Mutual aid arrives from far away

phaseArc.title: Recovery of capacity
phaseArc.goal: Resources are released and the system reconstitutes.
beats: Fires elsewhere are contained and resources are released
The preparedness level falls
Staff fatigue and rest rules apply

decisionPointExamples: move the last two engines to the north subdivision or hold them at the school
warn the east zones earlier because no engines can protect them
accept a partly filled order now or hold for a complete strike team
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a coordination center resource status, an unfilled order number, a preparedness level change, a crew rest requirement
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: an order that is canceled, an engine out of service, a fuel truck delay, a helicopter grounded by smoke
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the interagency dispatch or coordination center and the state fire agency
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: National preparedness levels run from 1 to 5; at level 5 resources are below drawdown levels for multiple resource types. State resource orders by number and status (filled, partly filled, unable to fill).

addedThreatFamilies.label: Flood and debris flow after a fire
addedThreatFamilies.description: A burn scar sheds water and debris at rainfall rates far below normal; the evacuation zones of the fire become flash flood and debris flow zones and the same agencies must switch from fire to flood language.

phaseArc.title: Burn scar and first rain forecast
phaseArc.goal: The fire is contained, and a forecast of rain over the burn scar starts the flood and debris flow planning.
beats: The weather service forecasts thunderstorms over the burn scar
The county reviews its burn scar flood plan and the zones below the scar
A school below the scar asks about bus routes

phaseArc.title: Watch and pre-positioning
phaseArc.goal: A flash flood watch with a burn scar tag sets the clock for road closures and notices.
beats: A flash flood watch names the burn scar
Public works stages barricades and a loader
Residents in former fire zones ask what applies to them

phaseArc.title: Warning and debris flows
phaseArc.goal: A warning with a considerable or catastrophic damage tag is issued and the thresholds are crossed within minutes.
beats: Rainfall rates cross the debris flow threshold
A flash flood warning with a burn scar tag is issued
A road below the scar is covered by debris

phaseArc.title: Closures, recovery and reopening
phaseArc.goal: Roads, power and water are restored and the zones are reopened in steps.
beats: A canyon road stays closed for days
Residents ask when they can return home
The next storm forecast is issued

decisionPointExamples: close the canyon road at the rainfall threshold or at the warning
order the zones below the scar to leave on a forecast, or wait for the warning and risk the clearance time
reopen the road after the storm or wait for the debris assessment
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a rain gauge reading above the threshold, a debris assessment map, a radar rainfall rate over the scar
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a gauge that burned in the fire, a road with a washed out culvert, a cell site on a burned pole
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the National Weather Service forecast office and the county public works department
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Use the flooding and debris flow toolkits for rainfall thresholds and warning tags; do not invent thresholds. The same zone ids from the fire may be reused for the flood and the zone status words are those of the project.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Wildfire alerting and communications degradation
addedThreatFamilies.description: The tools that warn and coordinate fail or mislead during a fire: an alerting platform outage, a dispatch or radio failure, cell and power loss in a canyon, a wrong or missed zone message, a utility notification failure or misinformation about orders.

phaseArc.title: First signs of failure
phaseArc.goal: A first message or tool behaves wrongly while the fire grows.
beats: The alert platform shows a delivery delay
A resident posts that they received no message
A dispatcher reports radio dead spots in a canyon

phaseArc.title: Wrong or missing messages
phaseArc.goal: A zone message goes to the wrong zone or not at all and the partners disagree.
beats: An order reaches the wrong zone
The county and the sheriff repeat different zone lists
A utility notice goes out an hour late

phaseArc.title: Workarounds
phaseArc.goal: Players use sweeps, sirens, radio and social media to reach people.
beats: Door-to-door sweeps replace text alerts in one zone
A social media rumor names zones that are not under order
The utility calls medical baseline customers by hand

phaseArc.title: Correction and review
phaseArc.goal: A correction goes out and the failure is documented.
beats: A correction message is sent through all channels
The platform is restored
The after-action list of gaps is started

decisionPointExamples: send a correction now through every channel, or confirm the cause first
use a sweep in the zone with no cell coverage, or wait for the platform to return
tell the public the system failed, or describe only what to do
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a delivery report with a zone count lower than expected, a resident's screenshot, a log time stamp that disagrees with the sent time
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a vendor support line that is closed, an incorrect polygon in the platform, a battery site that fails, a call center without a list
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the alert platform vendor, the dispatch center and the telecom provider
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Describe failures by their effect on who was reached and when. Keep zone ids and status words identical in every channel and say which zone each message addressed.

noiseExamples: a dispatcher's question about a routine burn permit
a vendor asking about hose replacement pricing
a notice of a training class schedule
a question about a fireworks ordinance
pressureExamples: a resident posting the wrong evacuation zone on a neighborhood app
a county commissioner asking whether to evacuate before the fire is closer
a TV station showing a perimeter that differs from the incident map
a homeowner demanding an engine for a house outside the priority list
a care home asking for transport before an order
a hospital asking the utility to keep power on a circuit that is scheduled for shutoff
an elected official criticizing the shutoff decision
